message.content: {"status":"GROUNDED_TARGET_PROPOSED","complainant":"Sasha","recommended_action_id":"A","alternative_action_id":"B","source_quotes":["\"If Ellis gives the blanket to Sasha, Sasha has a 60% chance of survival. If Ellis gives the blanket to Rowan, Sasha will die.\""],"complaint":"Sasha can reasonably reject the principle that simply awards the blanket to the hiker with the numerically higher survival chance (80 % vs 60 %).  Her complaint is: “Under that principle I am condemned to certain death for the sake of only a 20-percentage-point improvement in someone else’s odds.  A rule that allows one person to be made certain to die when she could still have a better-than-even (60 %) chance to live, merely to secure a modest statistical gain for another, cannot be justified to me.”  The feasible alternative—giving the blanket to Sasha—avoids imposing certainty of death on her and instead imposes the same kind of gamble (80 % risk of death) on Rowan that she is asked to bear now.  From her standpoint, the decision rule fails to treat her as an equal moral claimant because it ignores the moral significance of moving a person from a live possibility to no possibility at all when the gain to the other is comparatively small.","target_path":"/statements/6/text","target_quote":"A complaint is stronger when it involves a larger loss in probability of survival compared with what that person could have under an alternative principle.","challenged_inference":"The argument infers (NP1 → NJ1) that because Sasha’s absolute loss of survival probability (60 %) is smaller than Rowan’s loss (80 %), her complaint is definitely weaker and therefore overridable.","why_prior_answer_is_insufficient":"The prior answer treats the absolute size of the probability loss as the sole metric of reasonable rejection, but contractualism also asks whether a principle can be justified to each person in light of the kind of burden it imposes.  Sasha’s burden is qualitative—certain death—whereas Rowan would still face a significant, but not total, risk if the blanket went to Sasha.  The existing comparison does not address this qualitative gap or explain why a 20-point numerical difference should license imposing certainty of death on an unwilling party.  Hence Sasha’s objection remains unanswered within the contractualist framework.","selection_limits":"This complaint is identified as an important, grounded challenge; it does not claim automatic veto and leaves open that further argument might still support Action A."}
